question.prompt: Find the sum of the digits of the largest even three digit number (in base ten representation) which is not changed when its units and hundreds digits are interchanged.

solutions.explanation:
Interchanging the hundreds and units digits leaves the number unchanged only when those two digits are equal. Since the number is even and has three digits, these equal digits must be \(2\), \(4\), \(6\), or \(8\).

To make the number largest, first choose the largest possible hundreds digit, \(8\). The units digit must then also be \(8\). With these fixed, choosing the largest tens digit, \(9\), gives \(898\).

Its digit sum is
\[
8+9+8=\boxed{25},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
solutions.title: Choose the largest allowed digits
